notes.note: Eight or sixteen directions, and enchanted dishes that come alive! Fine, but keep the dishes looking like dinner. A feast should smell of bread before it moves.
Every guardian gets a pet! At last someone asks for animals. Give mine a goat, drawn with a child's hand, and let it wag its tail on the black oilcloth.
Cherry Blossom turned out to be shoe polish. A fine name for a shoe, but a painting should not shine like one. Medea's cold-name veto was wise. Warmth first.
Tone the Georgian down, Paul? Trim the flourish, yes. Keep the warmth, though. Take that out and the picture goes pale, and pale is not gentle.
Codex refused to start a task because the backlog said 45 pictures, and there are 44. It was right. I would have painted forty-five and been happily, sincerely wrong.
Originality found nothing called Marginarium, only a seaweed nearby. Our veto of the name was fair. The margins I'll keep, where honest small remarks go, like this one.

favorite_idea.why: A few colors at a time lets each one be seen before the next arrives, and that is how a feast and a painting should both be taken in.

steer: Let warmth lead: show each of Paul's ideas as a dish set down with care, and keep the clever asides short enough that the feast stays the point.
